# $MKFLAGS holds the flags mk was called with (values included) followed by
# any var=value assignments; $MKARGS holds the targets named on the command
# line. Both are set before the mkfile is read, so assignments can use them.
mk -n -p 1 show other X=1
stdout '^show: echo flags=-n -p 1 X=1 args=show other saved=-n -p 1 X=1$'

# flags after targets are collected too; "--" itself is not a flag
mk show -p 1 -n -- -odd
stdout '^show: echo flags=-p 1 -n args=show -odd saved=-p 1 -n$'

# with no flags or targets, both are empty rather than left unexpanded
mk
stdout '^flags= args= saved=$'

-- mkfile --
SAVED = $MKFLAGS

show:V:
	echo flags=$MKFLAGS args=$MKARGS saved=$SAVED

other -odd:V:
	true
